newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN Security Council to meet on Zaire force.
newsitem.headline: UN Security Council to meet on Zaire force.

text.p: Security Council members early on Saturday were set to adopt a resolution that lays the groundwork for a multinational force to help end the crisis in eastern Zaire.

But the resolution before the council would delay final approval of a force. Diplomats said the United States needed more time to see whether it would participate and if so, whether it would provide logistics, financial asssistance or other contributions.

The council earlier lowered its sights from supporting a French proposal that would authorise the immediate creation of a force to enable humanitarian supplies to be distributed among more than a million refugees from ethnic violence.

As a holding measure, U.N. members would be asked to prepare for early authorisation by the Security Council of a multinational force and to report back to the council as soon as possible. Another resolution would be needed to give the final go-ahead.
France and Spain have already said they could send 1,000 men each. However, Rwanda's Tutsi government is mistrustful of France as an ally of the ousted Hutu government.
Zaire has said it would no longer allow Rwandan and Burundian refugees to re-establish camps on its territory and that they must be repatriated.

Hundreds of thousands of people fled to eastern Zaire after genocidal massacres of Tutsis and moderate Hutus in Rwanda in 1994 while thousands more escaped continuing violence between Hutus and Tutsis in neighbouring Burundi.
